1 import SixVertexUnfolding.Geometry.CutEdgeTriangles
2 import SixVertexUnfolding.Geometry.SmallPolyhedronCutEdgeStrips
3 import SixVertexUnfolding.Geometry.SmallPolyhedronCutEdgeTriangleDevelopments
4 
5 /-! Keep the two actual radial developments of a cut edge together.
6 All fields are supplied by the existing geometric constructions.
7 
8 Here the shortest-route inputs come from the actual vertex fans of a
9 polyhedron with at most six vertices and triangular/quadrilateral faces.
10 No canonical graph model is assumed. -/
11 
12 namespace SixVertexUnfolding.ConvexPolyhedron
13 
14 open Set
15 
16 variable {P : ConvexPolyhedron} (size : P.vertices.card ≤ 6)
17   (small_faces : ∀ F : P.Face, (F.val ∩ (P.vertices : Set Space)).ncard = 3 ∨
18     (F.val ∩ (P.vertices : Set Space)).ncard = 4)
19 
20 include size small_faces in
21 /-- Both complete radial triangles exist for every actual cut-tree edge. -/
22 theorem small_exists_cut_edge_triangles (a : frontier P.body) (T : P.CutLocusTree a)
23     {u v : T.vertices} (edge : T.graph.Adj u v) : Nonempty (CutEdgeTriangles T edge) := by
24   obtain ⟨strips⟩ := small_exists_cut_edge_strips size small_faces a T edge
25   obtain ⟨model, first, second, agrees, member, ⟨D⟩, ⟨E⟩⟩ :=
26     small_exists_cut_edge_triangle_developments size small_faces a T edge strips
27   exact ⟨⟨strips, model, first, second, agrees, member, D, E⟩⟩
28 
29 end SixVertexUnfolding.ConvexPolyhedron
